content:
This is a recently discovered bug. The symptom happens when you previously attached a file but now the previous containing folder no longer exists because it was deleted or renamed. When you later try to attach a file using the Write window's "Attach" button, it will silently fail, that is, clicking the button will appear to do nothing. The bug has been fixed for the newest release, available now.

Otherwise, a workaround is to drag-and-drop the file onto the Write window using the mouse.

Or, if you're comfortable delving into Thunderbird's Advanced Settings:

- In <Settings | General | Config Editor> search for: "mail.compose.attach.dir".

- The value (path) here must be changed to one that is still available (for example C:\).

- The Attach button should work again right away - it's not necessary to restart Thunderbird.

Not sure what OS you are using and not sure what you are copying between computers.

So this is some info on the entire process I would recommend using when wanting to move from one computer to another.

To ensure your profile and mail accounts contain all data: (Not a real concern if you use IMAP as emails are stored on server and can be downloaded again)

But to make sure all is download do this:

  • Account Settings > Synchronisation & Storage for the account
  • Select 'Keep messages in all folders......'
  • Click on 'Advanced' button
  • make sure all folders and subfolders are selected and click on OK
  • Under 'Disk Space'
  • Select 'Synchronise all messages locally regardless of age'
  • Do not select any of the other two options.

Make sure all IMAP accounts have been set up as above.

Now to check you are fully up to date: In Thunderbird

  • Enable the Menu Bar if it's not already enabled.
  • Menu app icon (3 lines) > View > Toolbars > select 'Menu Bar'
  • In Menu Bar:
  • File > Offline > Download/Synch now
  • Select 'Mail messages'
  • If required select 'Newsgroup messages'
  • click on 'Select' and make sure everything is selected and click on Ok
  • then click on 'OK' to launch the synchronise.

Once completed - info will display in bottom Status bar

Then you can Exit Thunderbird and perform the manual copy/backup of the 'Thunderbird' folder that contains everything you need to move to another folder.

If you use Windows OS I created this question:

  • https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/questions/1587693

That 'Thunderbird' folder contains everything. So on new computer: download and install Thunderbird I suggest you download from the Thunderbird website : https://www.thunderbird.net/en-US/thunderbird/all/ install and let it launch so it creates a profile, then Exit Thunderbird.

Access the appropriate location where profile is stored:

So if in: C: Users/User name/Appdata/Roaming/Thunderbird Delete that 'Thunderbird' folder then paste the copied/backed up 'Thunderbird' folder into the 'Roaming' folder. Start Thunderbird

content:
It's a relatively common occurrence with a few of the more well-known AV apps (but not Windows Defender). The usual advice to prevent the problem is:

- set your AV app not to scan incoming messages

- enable this TB setting: TB menu > Settings > Privacy & Security > Security > Antivirus > Allow antivirus clients to quarantine individual incoming messages.

Then you will still be protected. It seems counter-intuitive but it works. What happens is that when a message is downloaded, it opens a temporary file in a folder where it's scanned by the AV app. If a problem is found with that message, the downloading continues uninterrupted.
